entries.appliesTo: health insurers, HMOs, and dental preferred-provider-plan insurers downcoding health benefits claims (providers also barred from unreviewed automated claim submission)

dutySources.human-review: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 9(a) — 'An insurer may not use an automated: (1) process; (2) system; or (3) tool, including artificial intelligence; as the sole basis to downcode a claim based on medical necessity without the review of the covered individual's medical record by an employee or contractor of the insurer.'
dutySources.disclosure-ui: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 9(c) — 'An insurer must disclose in an easily accessible and readable manner when artificial intelligence is used to: (1) make an adverse determination on a prior authorization request; or (2) downcode a claim.'
dutySources.takedown-process: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 12(a) — 'An insurer shall provide providers with a clear and accessible process for appealing downcoded claims, including: (1) a written or electronic notice detailing how to initiate an appeal'

exposure.enforcer: department (rulemaking under IC 4-22-2; no penalty stated for the downcoding chapter)

sources.humanReview: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 9(a) — 'without the review of the covered individual's medical record by an employee or contractor of the insurer'
sources.disclosure: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 9(c) — 'An insurer must disclose in an easily accessible and readable manner when artificial intelligence is used'
sources.aiSoleBasis: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 9(a) — 'may not use an automated: (1) process; (2) system; or (3) tool, including artificial intelligence; as the sole basis to downcode a claim based on medical necessity'
sources.appealDays: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 12(a)(3) — 'a timeline for submission of an appeal that is not less than one hundred eighty (180) days'
sources.enforcer: IC 27-1-52 Sec. 14 — 'The department shall adopt rules under IC 4-22-2 to carry out this chapter.'

flags: decisionsCovered enum mismatch: the AI sole-basis prohibition covers claim downcoding based on medical necessity and the AI disclosure covers prior-authorization adverse determinations and downcoded claims — neither maps cleanly to denials|prior-auth|all, so the param is omitted.

Sec. 9(b) imposes a mirror duty on providers, not insurers: 'A provider may not use an automated: (1) process; (2) system; or (3) tool, including artificial intelligence; to submit a health benefits claim without the review of a provider or other person involved in the development of the claim'.
The appeal process and 180-day appealDays (Sec. 12) apply to all downcoded claims, not only AI-assisted downcoding; batch appeals of similar claims must be allowed (Sec. 12(b)).
Chapter exclusion: 'This chapter does not apply to the Medicaid program or a managed care organization' (IC 27-1-52 Sec. 0.3).

Non-AI provisions outside the insurance-adm segment: hospital payment-assistance-program notice duties (IC 16-21-9.5) carrying a civil penalty of 'not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000) per violation' assessed by the state department; downcoding notice via CARC/RARC codes (Sec. 11); no targeted/discriminatory downcoding (Sec. 13); no downcoding based solely on diagnosis code (Sec. 10); 60-day notice before CPT rate reductions (IC 27-8-5.7-6.7, IC 27-13-36.2-4.7); 180-day recoupment and 3-year audit limits (IC 27-8-5.7-10, IC 27-13-36.2-8); coordination-of-benefits resubmission rights (IC 27-8-5.7-11.5, IC 27-13-36.2-9.5).
The downcoding chapter states no monetary penalty; the $1,000 penalty in the bill belongs to the hospital notice chapter (IC 16-21-9.5 Sec. 9) and is not imported into exposure.
